speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you'll find that with a lot of AI products.

zh: 一定有什么不对劲。

en: But then there are other functions like executive assistants, chiefs of staff, HR team members, finance, some more junior finance team members that don't have that much AI in their day-to-day.
zh: 但也有一些其他职能，比如行政助理、幕僚长、HR 团队成员、财务——一些比较初级的财务团队成员——他们的日常工作中没有那么多 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: They like really don't.
zh: 他们真的没有。

zh: 所以像 Town 这样的产品，我认为我们经常在这种地方发现早期采用和增长。

en: And I would say like some functions that seem from the outside like less juicy, but actually that are really hungry for technology to help make their life easier.
zh: 我想说的是，一些职能从外部看起来没那么吸引人，但实际上非常渴望有技术来帮助让他们的生活更轻松。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as soon as they adopt it, there's an interesting effect because they often work with like leaders or execs or people in ops teams.
zh: 所以一旦他们采用它，就会产生一个有趣的效果，因为他们经常与领导者、高管或运营团队的人一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we get penetration through the op teams.
zh: 然后我们就通过运营团队获得了渗透。

speaker: Unknown
en: How important is time to wow or time to user delight?
zh: 到惊艳的时长（time to wow），或到用户愉悦的时长有多重要？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 是的，老实说，我认为我们的产品今天能成立，唯一的原因就是我们单个用户的 time to value 非常低。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we give you time to value there really quickly?
zh: 我们能不能非常快地给你 time to value？

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们围绕真正建立人类与 AI 之间的这种关系，打造了一整套品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for a lot of our users that resonates, like they want that.

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have that.

zh: 我们还押注于网络效应，这个我们已经聊了很多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the third bet that we make is we are big believers that through a lot of pre-processing, you can get better outcomes for users.
zh: 然后我们做的第三个押注是，我们坚信通过大量的预处理，可以为用户带来更好的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we spend a lot of compute before you even ask a question to build a mental model of the user, like pre-creating context in a way that allows us to be really effective at things like work networking, understanding the projects that you're working on, understanding your company and those kinds of building blocks.

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are like three things that we think over time make a difference for a product.
zh: 所以这就是我们认为随着时间推移会对产品产生影响的三个方面。

en: So the question, if I were an investor, is like, why does someone deserve to win in Europe?
zh: 所以问题来了，如果我是一个投资者，我会问：为什么某家公司配得上在欧洲赢？

en: And is it a distribution thing?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 是 GDPR 和隐私的问题吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you said, GrokBot earlier.
zh: 就像你之前提到的 GrokBot。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they going to be able to have a war chest that's big enough to just keep up with capabilities?

en: And then do I believe they have a reason to win in this very horizontal market like where they are?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 市场的速度太疯狂了,Harry。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never seen anything like it.
zh: 我从没见过这样的东西。

en: Before, in the past, you talk to customers, you build a feature, they would use it, and you would be like learning from that feature.

en: You know, for startups, usually you're like milking these user insights for a really long time.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really good.

en: So I'm always like, you know, whenever I talk to him, I'm sad that we're competing, you know, we're competing.
zh: 所以每次我和他交谈,我都很伤心我们在竞争,你知道吗,我们在竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, that guy's good.
zh: 而我会想,那家伙很厉害。

speaker: Unknown
